item.text: The starter is a blank page with a small mock product source. I’m turning that into a browsable catalog and wrapping the shared product read in a tagged persistent cache. The sync action will use Next’s `"max"` revalidation profile, so the action returns promptly while catalog reads refresh with stale-while-revalidate behavior.

The catalog now uses a single shared cached product read, and the page’s sync form invalidates that same `products` tag with stale-while-revalidate semantics. I’ve also added server-rendered search/category filtering and a queued-sync message so the action preserves the current view and returns a visible response.

item.text:
Implemented the admin product catalog page with cached catalog reads, searchable/category-filtered products, inventory metrics, and a regular HTML form wired to an inline Server Action.

The shared product read in [lib/products.ts](/workspace/lib/products.ts) uses the `"products"` cache tag. The action revalidates that tag with Next.js’s `"max"` profile, so it can return promptly while stale data is served and refreshed in the background for views using the shared read.

The starter has no ERP/PIM connector, so the action refreshes the cached product source; [lib/db.js](/workspace/lib/db.js) still contains sample data. I did not run tests or a build.
